name: exp3-r3-incumbent-residuals
description: Exp3 round 3 MAP tests of single changes to upward_count_start_boundary; which cues help and which do nothing
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 round 3 (2026-10-18), incumbent upward_count_start_boundary MAP ll −4642.8. Fitted weights: size w≈0.69 per 100 units (weak), graded-factor w≈0.005 (factor similarity basically unused).
Changes tested, MAP ll gain each: isolation memory, where an example differing from the rest in parity and digit weighs more (+6.6, submitted as distinctive_example_isolation_memory); a tens-digit/decade similarity dimension (+5.6); factor-mismatch normalisation variants with max, geometric mean, or 1 having no factors (0 or worse); exp(-d^q) similarity shape (+0.3).
Residuals left over: targets 1 and 2 over-predicted by about 0.07; set-level yes-rate SD is 0.147 observed vs 0.114 predicted.
**Why:** saves re-testing dead ends. Gains this small (~5 nats) probably come out below 1 dse in ELPD.
**How to apply:** skip factor-similarity tweaks. The decade dimension is still untried as its own candidate. See [[residual-ascending-below-start]] for the workflow (scratch/resid.py in iter_3/candidate_4).

name: order-effects-exhausted
description: Exp3 r3 MAP screen — order mechanisms beyond the upward start boundary gain at most ~2 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
On 2026-10-18 (exp3 round 3) I MAP-fit upward_count_start_boundary (ll −4642.8) and tested order variants. First-example primacy boost gained 2.0 nats (submitted as primacy_recency_serial_position; retention went 0.91→0.77, primacy 0.5). Rehearsal weighting gained 1.7. Coherence from last-anchored pairs gained 1.3. Continuing the last step forward gained 1–1.7. A first- or last-anchored partial span, and successive-pair or first-anchored coherence, gained nothing or lost fit. The largest remaining misfit is set-level (e.g. 63,67, 53,47,41 and 3,33,99 are over-predicted; 31,19,49,100 is under-predicted), not order.
**Why:** this saves re-screening order effects in later rounds.
**How to apply:** for order-themed briefs, expect small gains. Look for bigger wins in set-level structure. Builds on [[residual-ascending-below-start]]. The scripts are in iter_3/candidate_0/scratch (fit.py and varA–K).

name: residual-ascending-below-start
description: Exp3 round 2 MAP residual finding — targets below the first example of ascending sets are over-predicted by the best model
metadata:
  type: project
---
In experiment3 round 2 (2026-10-18) a MAP fit of saturating_criterion_relaxation showed that targets below the first example of sets whose last example is larger than the first were over-predicted by about 0.1. Adding one all-or-none logit penalty for those targets improved the MAP log-likelihood by about 28 nats (−4671 to −4643). The symmetric "behind the start" version gained only about 6, and a graded version about 19. Targets 1 and 2 are also over-predicted by about 0.11 overall. This became candidate upward_count_start_boundary.
**Why:** a quick MAP fit plus grouped residuals (scratch/resid.py) finds targeted single mechanisms much faster than reading the critique alone.
**How to apply:** before proposing a candidate, MAP-fit the incumbent and group residuals by set and target structure.

Round 3 (2026-10-18): grafting the same penalty onto sample_size_neglect_range_inference raised its MAP log-likelihood from −4667 to −4639, about 4 better than the incumbent (−4643). The penalty fit at about 0.63 in both models, so it is roughly additive with range inference. This became candidate sample_size_neglect_upward_start.

name: round-base-multiples-prior
description: Exp3 r4 MAP screen on leading_digit_string_similarity — round-base prior for "multiples of g" gains ~10 nats; primes/powers/repdigit/lattice null
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 round 4 (2026-10-18). Incumbent leading_digit_string_similarity has a MAP log-likelihood of −4630.2. Its residuals show the multiples-of-g rule under-applied for g = 2, 4, 5, 8, 10 (on-target residual +0.05 to +0.13) and over-applied for g = 3, 6, 9 (−0.03 to −0.06).
- Extend the rule to g ≥ 2 and add a signed "round base" prior term, where round means g divides 100 or g is a power of 2: −4619.7 (+10.5). Submitted as round_base_multiples_prior (iter_4/candidate_0).
- The round-base prior alone with g ≥ 3: +6.8. Extending to g ≥ 2 alone: +3.6.
- Null or small: a prime rule (+1.3); a powers-of-b rule (0); repdigit sets (too few data); a step-lattice rule for uncovered sets (roughly 0).
Leftover residuals: target 1 is still over-predicted in many sets; the set-level SD is 0.147 observed vs 0.118 predicted.
**Why:** saves re-screening concept additions.
**How to apply:** the scripts are in iter_4/candidate_0/scratch (mapv.py, grp.py, gg.py, lat.py). See [[exp3-r3-residual-scan]].
Refinement of leading_digit_string_similarity (all else unchanged: recency-weighted similarity on size, final digit, parity, graded shared factor and leading written digit with coherence-stretched attention, the "multiples of g", "ends in d" and fixed-list concepts, the filled-in span, sequence momentum, zigzag breadth, the saturating criterion relaxation and the upward-count start boundary). The single change, taken from even_number_rule_abstraction, is that "even numbers" is an explicit rule people abstract: when every example is even they consult "the program makes even numbers" as separate evidence at the decision, weighted by how unlikely it is that that many examples would all be even by chance, so after all-even sets far-away even targets are endorsed and nearby odd targets rejected more than parity similarity predicts. "Odd" is the unmarked leftover category and evokes no such rule, producing the even-versus-odd set asymmetry the critique reports.

"""Leading-digit string similarity exemplar model.

Refinement of upward_count_start_boundary (all else unchanged). The single
change: people also compare numbers as written digit strings by their leading
digit. A target whose first written digit matches an example's (34 after 31
or 3) feels more similar to that example, all-or-none, with attention to this
match stretched when the examples share a leading digit, so targets sharing
the examples' leading digit are endorsed more than numerical distance alone
predicts.
"""
import math
from functools import reduce

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt

MAXK = 4
NDIM = 5  # magnitude, final digit, parity, graded shared factor, leading digit
SESSION_LEN = 450.0


def _factor_mismatch(t, x):
    m = min(t, x)
    if m <= 1:
        return 0.0
    return 1.0 - math.log(math.gcd(t, x)) / math.log(m)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    n = len(rows)
    mism = np.ones((n, NDIM, MAXK))
    coh = np.zeros((n, NDIM))
    lag = np.zeros((n, MAXK))
    mask = np.zeros((n, MAXK))
    rule = np.zeros(n)
    digit_rule = np.zeros(n)
    position = np.zeros(n)
    ahead = np.zeros(n)
    below_start = np.zeros(n)
    disorder = np.zeros(n)
    is_example = np.zeros(n)
    rating = np.zeros(n, dtype="int64")
    cache = {}
    for r, row in enumerate(rows):
        s = str(row["number_set"])
        ex = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")][:MAXK]
        t = int(row["target"])
        k = len(ex)
        if s not in cache:
            pairs = [(ex[i], ex[j]) for i in range(k) for j in range(i + 1, k)]
            c = np.zeros(NDIM)
            if pairs:
                c[0] = np.mean([max(0.0, 1.0 - abs(a - b) / 50.0) for a, b in pairs])
                c[1] = np.mean([a % 10 == b % 10 for a, b in pairs])
                c[2] = np.mean([a % 2 == b % 2 for a, b in pairs])
                c[3] = np.mean([1.0 - _factor_mismatch(a, b) for a, b in pairs])
                c[4] = np.mean([str(a)[0] == str(b)[0] for a, b in pairs])
            g = reduce(math.gcd, ex) if k >= 2 else 0
            d = ex[0] % 10 if k >= 2 and len({x % 10 for x in ex}) == 1 else -1
            cache[s] = (c, g, d)
        c, g, d = cache[s]
        if d >= 0:
            digit_rule[r] = (k - 1) * math.log(10.0) * (1.0 if t % 10 == d else -1.0)
        coh[r] = c
        is_example[r] = 1.0 if t in ex else 0.0
        if g >= 3:
            rule[r] = (k - 1) * math.log(g) * (1.0 if t % g == 0 else -1.0)
        # +1 beyond the last example in the direction of travel, -1 behind
        # the start, 0 inside the span or with no direction (one example).
        travel = (ex[-1] > ex[0]) - (ex[-1] < ex[0])
        out = (t > max(ex)) - (t < min(ex))
        ahead[r] = float(travel * out)
        # Below the starting point of an upward-counting sequence (the change).
        below_start[r] = 1.0 if (travel > 0 and t < ex[0]) else 0.0
        # Share of direction reversals between successive steps in shown
        # order (0 monotone, 1 full zigzag), centred; 0 with fewer than 3.
        if k >= 3:
            steps = [b - a for a, b in zip(ex, ex[1:])]
            revs = [(a > 0) != (b > 0) for a, b in zip(steps, steps[1:])]
            disorder[r] = float(np.mean(revs)) - 0.5
        for i, x in enumerate(ex):
            mism[r, 0, i] = max(0, min(ex) - t, t - max(ex)) / 100.0
            mism[r, 1, i] = 0.0 if t % 10 == x % 10 else 1.0
            mism[r, 2, i] = 0.0 if t % 2 == x % 2 else 1.0
            mism[r, 3, i] = _factor_mismatch(t, x)
            # Leading written digit match (the change).
            mism[r, 4, i] = 0.0 if str(t)[0] == str(x)[0] else 1.0
            lag[r, i] = k - 1 - i
            mask[r, i] = 1.0
        ti = row.get("trial_index")
        if ti is not None and str(ti).strip() != "":
            position[r] = min(max(float(ti), 0.0), SESSION_LEN) / SESSION_LEN
        rv = row.get("rating")
        rating[r] = int(float(rv)) if rv is not None and str(rv).strip() != "" else 0
    return {"mismatch": mism, "coherence": coh, "lag": lag, "ex_mask": mask,
            "rule_evidence": rule, "digit_rule_evidence": digit_rule,
            "session_position": position, "ahead": ahead, "below_start": below_start,
            "disorder": disorder, "is_example": is_example, "rating": rating}


with pm.Model() as model:
    mismatch = pm.Data("mismatch", np.zeros((1, NDIM, MAXK)))
    coherence = pm.Data("coherence", np.zeros((1, NDIM)))
    lag = pm.Data("lag", np.zeros((1, MAXK)))
    ex_mask = pm.Data("ex_mask", np.ones((1, MAXK)))
    rule_evidence = pm.Data("rule_evidence", np.zeros(1))
    digit_rule_evidence = pm.Data("digit_rule_evidence", np.zeros(1))
    session_position = pm.Data("session_position", np.zeros(1))
    ahead = pm.Data("ahead", np.zeros(1))
    below_start = pm.Data("below_start", np.zeros(1))
    disorder = pm.Data("disorder", np.zeros(1))
    is_example = pm.Data("is_example", np.zeros(1))

    w_base = pm.HalfNormal("w_base", sigma=np.array([10.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0, 2.0]))
    tuning = pm.HalfNormal("tuning", sigma=2.0, shape=NDIM)
    retention = pm.Beta("retention", alpha=2.0, beta=2.0)
    bias = pm.Normal("bias", mu=-1.0, sigma=2.0)
    gain = pm.HalfNormal("gain", sigma=5.0)
    rule_weight = pm.HalfNormal("rule_weight", sigma=1.0)
    digit_rule_weight = pm.HalfNormal("digit_rule_weight", sigma=1.0)
    # How far the yes-criterion relaxes from session start to end.
    criterion_drift = pm.Normal("criterion_drift", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    # Time constant of the relaxation, as a share of the session:
    # small = fast early relaxation then plateau; large = nearly linear.
    relax_tau = pm.Beta("relax_tau", alpha=2.0, beta=4.0)
    relax_shape = ((1.0 - pt.exp(-session_position / relax_tau))
                   / (1.0 - pt.exp(-1.0 / relax_tau)))
    # Evidence from the "fixed list of these numbers" concept.
    list_weight = pm.HalfNormal("list_weight", sigma=2.0)

    # Evidence against numbers below an upward sequence's start (the change).
    start_penalty = pm.HalfNormal("start_penalty", sigma=2.0)

    # Momentum: shrinks size mismatch ahead of the sequence, stretches it behind.
    momentum = pm.Normal("momentum", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    # Zigzag: a disorderly sequence shrinks the size mismatch.
    zigzag_sensitivity = pm.Normal("zigzag_sensitivity", mu=0.0, sigma=1.0)
    size_scale = pt.exp(-momentum * ahead - zigzag_sensitivity * disorder)
    mismatch = pt.set_subtensor(
        mismatch[:, 0, :], mismatch[:, 0, :] * size_scale[:, None])

    attn = w_base[None, :] * pt.exp(tuning[None, :] * coherence)
    dist = pt.sum(attn[:, :, None] * mismatch, axis=1)
    sim = pt.exp(-dist)
    mem = ex_mask * pt.exp(lag * pt.log(retention))
    mem = mem / pt.sum(mem, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    familiarity = pt.sum(mem * sim, axis=1)

    logit = (bias + criterion_drift * relax_shape + gain * familiarity
             + rule_weight * rule_evidence
             + digit_rule_weight * digit_rule_evidence
             + list_weight * is_example
             - start_penalty * below_start)
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic(
        "p_yes", pt.clip(pm.math.sigmoid(logit), 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))

    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)

I wrote a new candidate for the repair slot, `trivial_small_number_avoidance`, and the admission check prints `OK`. It loads, the data contract holds, and a short MCMC fit completed with a finite log-likelihood of −4633.9. That check doesn't test novelty against the other models.

**Why the first attempt was rejected.** It grafted the "even numbers" rule onto the incumbent. Another slot this round had submitted exactly that graft (`leading_digit_even_rule_similarity`), so the predictions were near-identical. I dropped that idea.

**The new mechanism.** It refines `leading_digit_string_similarity` and keeps everything else unchanged. The one change: people believe a number-generating program doesn't produce the trivial bottom of the counting sequence. Targets 1, 2 and 3 are rejected more than their similarity to the examples predicts, whatever the set. The penalty is strongest at 1 and fades quickly above that; the rate of fading is fixed, and only its strength is fitted.

**What the data showed.** In a quick best-fit pass on the incumbent, targets 1 and 2 were over-predicted by about 0.07 (279 and 207 responses). I compared several single changes against the incumbent's log-likelihood of −4630.2:

| Change tried | Gain (nats) |
|---|---|
| Penalty fading from target 1 (submitted) | +6.5 |
| All-or-none penalty on targets 1–3 | +6.8 |
| Penalty on targets 1 and 2 only | +6.2 |
| Penalty on target 1 only | +3.5 |
| Criterion shift with number of examples | +2.5 |
| Criterion shift for all-odd sets | +1.5 |

**Two caveats:**
- **The gain is small.** About 6.5 nats at the best fit may well come out within one standard error of the incumbent in the full ELPD-LOO comparison.
- **It doesn't target the critique's flagged gaps.** It leaves set-level dispersion, the even-versus-odd asymmetry and the log-magnitude gap where they were.

**Novelty.** The change only moves predictions for very small targets. I estimate it clears the near-duplicate threshold (0.002) about tenfold, but that's an estimate, not a measurement.

I also saved these results to the memory notes, along with a reminder that popular grafts can collide with sibling slots.

Files are in `iter_4/candidate_4_repair_1/`:
- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
- `scratch/` (the screening scripts)
